title: Paramedic station needs and administrative penalties
subtitle: Also covered: internal audit work plan, enterprise risk management framework, and staff recognitions for leadership and museum work.
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended a new Administrative Penalty System for by-law enforcement. It covers the by-laws, hearing officer positions, policies and fees needed to run it {{vote:m2}}. The committee also recommended the Internal Audit Work Plan for 2025 to 2027 {{vote:m3}}. For 2025 it includes value-for-money reviews of facilities cleaning and of building permit approvals and inspections, plus a review of fleet maintenance.

The committee received the Enterprise Risk Management Policy and Framework Overview {{vote:m4}}. Staff plan to bring an enterprise risk register to Council in June 2025. Details of the risks are expected to be discussed in closed session, with some public reporting.

The committee also heard a presentation on the paramedic services deployment study, which was for information only and had no motion. It projects growing call volumes, a need for about 40 more paramedics over ten years, and new or relocated stations. Staff and the county will work through build-versus-lease options and report back ahead of the 2026 budget update. After a closed session, the Mayor reported that the committee received a cyber security briefing and gave staff direction on the Guelph Storm Hockey Club agreement.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the by-laws creating an Administrative Penalty System and screening and hearing officer positions, designating by-laws under it, adopting related policies, and adding the administrative fees to the User Fees By-law.
The committee recommended approving the work plan, which includes value-for-money reviews of facilities cleaning and building permit and inspection services, and a fleet maintenance review in 2025.
The committee received the Enterprise Risk Management Policy and Framework Overview for information.

debate: On risk management, one councillor asked why departments would phase in the framework over three years at 25, 50 and 75 percent uptake. Staff said the internal audit team is small and the work needs time and resources. They agreed to show at budget time what faster progress would require.

Councillors differed on transparency and reporting. One suggested a risk lens on every Council report, similar to the strategic plan alignment. Another said single reports would show only one piece of a larger picture, and the risk register is best discussed in private. Staff said much of the risk detail is confidential but they would look at public reporting, such as an annual report.

On the audit plan, councillors asked how areas for value-for-money reviews are chosen and how the building inspection review would treat customer service. Staff said Council input is welcome and the review would look at process and customer service risks as well as numbers.

On paramedic stations, one councillor questioned the roughly $1,390 per square foot budget figure. Staff said post-disaster building standards add reinforcement, seismic restraint and backup generation. Councillors also noted the study implies rising operating and capital costs. Staff said the build-versus-lease comparison has not yet been analyzed.

Councillors asked staff to explore co-locating stations with other county needs or housing, and to look at speeding up several identical-design stations to save money. Staff said the post-disaster standard complicates housing on top of a station, though separate buildings on one parcel may work. Staff also explained that modern stations need private space for showering and mental health decompression.
